## Survey open-0: LIN-4454 @ cfd152fa4

The ticket was grounded at 4b5001ddf. Since then `origin/main` has moved one commit, to cfd152fa4 (LIN-4453, docs only). It changes no code here, but it breaks one instruction.

**1. "Settles Waiting: 19" now points at the wrong entry.** LIN-4453 added a Waiting entry (`lib/run-ledger.js`: `landingPrUrls` skips only blind reads…), so every entry after it moved down one. At cfd152fa4, entry 19 is the close-out reasons entry (`lib/run-closeout-state.js`: the close-out reasons are bare string literals…). The `dispatchModelOf` entry is now 20 (`docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md:130`). Find the entry by its text, not its number. The Lessons clause to cut is at lines 55–56; Lessons is about 4.3 KB, well under the 6,144-byte limit.

**2. The witness only holds for a lineage with one dispatch.** The lane label is `session.model` (`lib/task-timeline.js:350`), which is the fold over the whole lineage. A row's model would be the fold over just that dispatch's records. In a multi-dispatch lineage the two can honestly differ, for example when a follow-up ran on Haiku. So write the Drift test as one dispatch: A has $5 priced plus one unpriced request, B has $1 priced, and both lane and row name A. With nothing priced, both name the latest model. Don't write it as "lane == every row", or someone will later "fix" a correct disagreement.

**3. The code change is small. The surrounding work is where the difficulty is.**
- `dispatchesOf` (`lib/cost-read.js:554`) already has `fold.last`. Add `model: fold.last.model` and leave the no-records branch as `model: null`, not a guess.
- `dispatches` is on the public wire (`routes/proxy-compute.js:712`, which says additive keys go last). `tests/unit/lin-4404-task-life-cost-read.test.js:93` pins the exact key order, so put `model` last and update that assertion. Also update the field list in `lib/proxy-instructions.js:404` and `docs/proxy-integration.md`.
- In `tests/unit/task-timeline.test.js`, the `d()` helper (line 34) builds dispatches with only `byModel`. Once rows read `dispatch.model`, every fixture shows null unless the helper also sets `model`. Check `tests/fixtures/task-timeline/lin-4393.js` too.
- Edge case: when nothing is priced, the fold names the latest record's model even if that model is `null`. The old rule filtered out null models. Accept the null and don't add a fallback, or you've written a second rule again.

**Symptom or cause?** It's mostly the cause, with one deeper layer. The fold already returns `byModel` in its own ranked order. `dispatchModelOf` re-sorted it, and because `modelRowOf` drops `pricedUsd`/`pricedRequests`, a reader can't reproduce the fold's rule from the wire anyway. Carrying the fold's answer is the right fix. Don't put the priced fields back on the wire, since that would invite re-ranking again.

**What I'd do first:** delete the right Waiting entry (item 1), then write the single-dispatch Drift test against `taskTimeline` fed from a real `readCost({perDispatch:true})` result, not from a hand-built `byModel`. After that, the change is about 3 lines plus the key-order assertion. Piece 7 edits other parts of `lib/cost-read.js` (`readCalls`/`callsSurfaceOf`), so a rebase should be mechanical.

## Survey global: LIN-4454 @ cfd152fa4

(One docs-only commit past the grounding 4b5001ddf. No code under this task has moved.)

**Where it lands.** Three files in a row: `lib/request-usage-fold.js` (the rule's home, 134 lines, pure, well documented), `lib/cost-read.js` (`dispatchesOf`, `modelRowOf`), and `lib/task-timeline.js` (`dispatchModelOf`, line 54). The cost read keeps getting tidier (LIN-4263 → 4276 → 4404 each gave a shared rule one home). The second copy came in with the new timeline (LIN-4405).

**What the drift really is.** It isn't just that the timeline re-ranks. `modelRowOf` projects the fold's model rows down to `{model, requests, tokens, costUsd}` and drops `pricedUsd`. So once the data is on the wire, no reader *can* rebuild the fold's rule. `dispatchModelOf` used the nearest field it had (`costUsd`, which is null when any request is unpriced, then request count), and so it got both the Drift case and the nothing-priced case wrong. Also undocumented: `byModel` already comes out in rank order, so `byModel[0].model` is nearly the fold's answer by accident. Don't lean on that. Carry `model` explicitly.

**Done the obvious way** (`model: fold.last.model` on each populated dispatch, `null` on the no-records branch, rows read `dispatch.model`), the change:
- adds one wire key per dispatch. It has to go last, after `lastRequestAt`. The exact key-order test (`tests/unit/lin-4404-task-life-cost-read.test.js:93`), the field list in `lib/proxy-instructions.js:404` and the shape/example in `docs/proxy-integration.md` (~1234, 1268) all spell out the shape. Only the test would notice. The docs would go quietly stale.
- leaves timeline tests with nothing to read from, because `d()` in `tests/unit/task-timeline.test.js:34` and `tests/fixtures/task-timeline/lin-4393.js` (14 `byModel` uses) feed the model only through `byModel`. They need a `model` field, or the rows go blank and the tests that assert a row model break.
- leaves one rule, in `foldRequestUsage`.

**Watch for:**
- In a multi-dispatch lineage, the lane label (the lineage fold) and a row (that dispatch's fold) can *legitimately* differ, for example a cheap follow-up under an expensive build. So the witness's "lane and row name the same model" only holds for a one-dispatch lane. Build it that way, through real `readCost({perDispatch:true})` → `taskTimeline`, so the test protects the rule, not a coincidence.
- "Settles Waiting: 19" is stale. Find the entry by its `dispatchModelOf` text (now at `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md:130`). In Lessons (lines 54–56), keep the rule sentence and drop the "`dispatchModelOf` … did, and a lane can now name two models" tail. Lessons is 4,258 bytes, well under the cap.

**Better, at a cost this task can carry:** add a sentence in `docs/proxy-integration.md` and in proxy-instructions saying that a dispatch's `model` follows the lineage's rule (cost-dominant priced model, else the latest). External readers then get the same "don't re-rank `byModel`" guidance the Lesson gives internal ones.

**Better still, not this task's:** decide whether `byModel` should carry `pricedUsd` (or say plainly that its order is the rank). Today the public per-model rows are missing the field the rule ranks by, so any outside reader is pushed toward the same mistake. Piece 7's move of `readCalls`/`callsSurfaceOf` out of `cost-read.js` is the natural moment to look at what that file projects.

## Implementation: PR open, CI green

**PR:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2425, branch `feat/lin-4454-model-from-fold`, targeting `main`. **Head:** `0b41e6d6d76fca15836d981528707e542e4b7742`. Not merged.

**CI:** all 8 checks pass on the head, including `CI success` (it covers Unit tests, Unit tests proxy/clock +400d, E2E shards 1–4, plus the separate source secret scan). Run: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/43451306234. Locally, `npm run test:unit` gives 25,283 pass and 0 fail.

**What the PR retires:**
- **`dispatchModelOf`** (`lib/task-timeline.js`) and its ranking by `costUsd`, then request count.
- **The Lessons clause naming it** in `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`. The rule sentence stays. Lessons goes from 4,269 to 4,182 bytes.
- **The Waiting entry about it**, found by its text: "`lib/task-timeline.js`: `dispatchModelOf` picks a dispatch's model by its own rule". It was entry 20 at cfd152fa4, not the 19 the ticket names. Waiting goes from 21 to 20.

**The change:**
- **`dispatchesOf` (`lib/cost-read.js`)** now carries the fold's answer: `model: fold.last.model`, or `null` when a dispatch has no records.
- **Timeline rows** read `dispatch.model`.
- **Wire:** one new **last** key, `model`, on each `dispatches[]` entry. It is also documented in `lib/proxy-instructions.js` and `docs/proxy-integration.md`, with a sentence telling readers not to re-rank `byModel`.
- **Unchanged:** `byModel` rows, which keep no priced fields.

**Witness** (`tests/unit/lin-4454-dispatch-model-from-fold.test.js`): the real `readCost({perDispatch:true})` result goes into `taskTimeline`, using **one dispatch** only. A lane folds the whole lineage and a row folds one dispatch, so in a lineage with several dispatches the two can honestly differ. The four cases:
1. **The Drift case:** model A has $5 priced plus one unpriced request, model B has $1 priced. Both name A.
2. **Nothing priced:** both name the latest model.
3. **Nothing priced, latest record has no model:** both read null, with no fallback.
4. **$0 priced model, later unpriced one:** both name the priced model, not `byModel[0]`.

**Evidence:**
- **Before the fix:** cases 1–3 were red on cfd152fa4, failing only on the row check (for example, the row said `'claude-haiku-5-5'` where the lane said `'claude-unrated-a'`).
- **Mutation checks:** making the row use the old ranking fails 3/4 cases; making it read `byModel[0]` fails case 4.

**Merge order with LIN-4457:** `feat/lin-4457-cost-read-calls-file` merges cleanly in code. It conflicts mechanically in `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`, because it adds a Lesson right after the one this PR shortens; keep both. Whichever PR lands second rebases.

## Review — LIN-4454

**PR:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2425. Reviewed at head `0b41e6d6d76fca15836d981528707e542e4b7742`. It is open, mergeable and not merged.

CI: green. All 8 checks pass on `0b41e6d6d`, including `CI success`: Unit, Unit (proxy, clock +400d), E2E shards 1–4, and the source secret scan.

**Re-grounding.** Since the ticket was created, `origin/main` has moved two commits, to `92676b1fe`. The first is `cfd152fa4` (LIN-4453, docs only). The second is LIN-4446 (cost formatter). Neither touches any of the PR's 10 files: `git log cfd152fa4..origin/main -- <PR files>` is empty. As both surveys found, the ticket's "Waiting 19" is stale. The PR deletes the right entry, found by its `dispatchModelOf` text.

### Against what was asked
- **Cause** (`dispatchModelOf` ranks by its own rule, and `dispatchesOf` drops `fold.last`): fixed at the cause. `dispatchesOf` (`lib/cost-read.js`) now carries `model: fold.last.model` on populated dispatches and `model: null` with no records. `dispatchRowOf` (`lib/task-timeline.js:66`) reads `dispatch.model ?? null`, and `dispatchModelOf` is deleted.
- **Approach:** met exactly. `byModel` rows are unchanged and gain no priced fields, as the survey constraint asks. The null case gets no fallback.
- **Retires:** `dispatchModelOf` and its ranking are gone. The Lessons tail that named it is cut, and the rule sentence stays. Lessons is 4,182 bytes, under 6,144. The Waiting entry is removed by its text, so Waiting now has 20 entries. The PR body has a "What this piece retires" section. One small gap: the builder posted no `### Leftovers` comment with a `Retires:` line. The implementation comment's "What the PR retires" block names the same entry, and the diff removes it, so the substance is met.
- **Witness:** `tests/unit/lin-4454-dispatch-model-from-fold.test.js` feeds a real `readCost({perDispatch:true})` result into `taskTimeline`, using one dispatch.
  - Case 1 is the Drift case: A has $5 priced plus one unpriced request, B has $1 priced, and both lane and row name A.
  - Case 2: with nothing priced, both name the latest model.
  - Case 3: when the latest record has a null model, both read null.
  - Case 4: a $0 priced model followed by an unpriced one. This case rules out reading `byModel[0]`.
  - Following the survey, the test is scoped to one dispatch. It correctly avoids asserting "lane == every row".
- **Binding constraints:** the model is computed on read from records, and nothing is stored. No GitHub or provider reads are added. No pre-cutover history is recomputed. No prompt changelog text is touched. The LLM & prompts side is untouched.
- **Wire:** `model` is added as the last key, after `lastRequestAt`. The exact-key-order test now covers both a populated dispatch and a dispatch with no records. `lib/proxy-instructions.js`, `docs/proxy-integration.md` and the JSDoc in `routes/proxy-compute.js` all document the field and say not to re-rank `byModel`. That covers the survey's "better, at a cost this task can carry" item.

### Mutation checks (run by me, all reverted, tree clean)
Baseline: the witness, `task-timeline.test.js` and `lin-4404-task-life-cost-read.test.js` run 48 pass, 0 fail.
- **M1:** `dispatchesOf` returns `model: null`. Witness cases 1, 2 and 4 go red, and so does the LIN-4404 key/value test. Case 3 stays green, as it should, because the right answer there is null.
- **M2:** `dispatchesOf` returns `fold.byModel[0].model`. Case 4 goes red, so the test does not pass by the `byModel`-order accident.
- **M3:** the timeline row ignores `dispatch.model` and returns null. Cases 1, 2 and 4 go red, so the witness really goes through the timeline. The builder also showed red results under the old ranking (3 of 4 cases) and on main before the fix.

### Regression check
`git log -30` on `lib/cost-read.js` and `lib/task-timeline.js` shows no reverts. The model-related history (LIN-4263, LIN-4177, LIN-4404, LIN-4405) is extended, not undone. The "dispatch with no records reads null, never 0" rule from LIN-4263 holds for `model` too.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
**Class:** a reader re-deriving a dispatch's or lineage's model instead of taking the fold's answer. I searched `lib/`, `routes/` and `public/` for `byModel` sorts, reductions and `[0]` reads, and for `.dispatches` consumers. The only other per-model sort is `lib/model-routing-spend.js`. It sums priced spend per *effective* model across jobs and does not choose one model, so it is a different rule. The only consumers of `dispatches` are `lib/task-timeline.js` and `render-task-timeline.js`, which renders `row.model` and does not rank. **This is an isolated change.** The surveys' "better still" item (whether `byModel` should carry `pricedUsd` or document its order) is **outside** this ticket. The surveys already pointed it at piece 7 (LIN-4457), so I file nothing new.

### Test level
The change crosses modules: the cost read, then the timeline, then the render. The witness is an integration test through the real `readCost` and `taskTimeline`. The existing e2e `tests/e2e/task-timeline.spec.js` drives dispatch rows on the task page, and it is green in CI. That level is appropriate.

### Checklist
Tests cover the new behaviour ✔. Fixtures are updated: `d()` sets `model`, and `lin-4393.js` is updated ✔. No security surface, since this only adds a read-side field ✔. The style matches the codebase ✔. There is no performance effect, because `fold.last` was already computed ✔.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **inside** (a claim this ticket's change depends on, its Lessons and Waiting edits). **Settle before the merge, only if LIN-4457 (PR on `feat/lin-4457-cost-read-calls-file`) lands first.** That PR conflicts mechanically in `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`, because it adds a Lesson right after the one this PR shortens. After the rebase, check all of the following:
  - The Lessons line ends at "…never re-ranks `byModel` itself. (Drift & Coherence Review…)" with no `dispatchModelOf` tail.
  - LIN-4457's new Lesson is still present.
  - No Waiting entry contains `dispatchModelOf`.
  - Lessons is under 6,144 bytes.
  - CI is green on the rebased head.

  If this PR lands first, the item passes to LIN-4457's rebase and is discharged here.

Apart from that item, CI covers the deliverable: the key order, the fold-to-timeline witness and the e2e dispatch rows.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

## Blind read
Verdict: better. It removes `dispatchModelOf` from `lib/task-timeline.js`. That function was a second ranking rule (by wire `costUsd`, then requests) that could disagree with the fold. Each dispatch's model now has one owner, `foldRequestUsage`'s `last.model`, carried by `dispatchesOf` in `lib/cost-read.js`, and `tests/unit/lin-4454-dispatch-model-from-fold.test.js` pins it through the real read. On the worse side, the change is small: one hand-built dispatch fixture in the timeline tests was not updated to the new entry shape.

Read: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2425 at `0b41e6d6d` against `cfd152fa4`.

### Inside the area, fix-sized
- `lib/task-timeline.js` (runs-and-dispatch): the `d` helper in `tests/unit/task-timeline-page.test.js` (the renderer's cost-gate test) still builds dispatch entries with a `byModel` model and no `model` key. `dispatchRowOf` now reads only `dispatch.model`, so every row in that test renders with no model, a shape the read never produces. The test still passes because it only checks cost words, but its input is now stale. The `tests/unit/task-timeline.test.js` helper was updated and this one was missed. Fix: add `model: 'claude-opus-5-5'` to that helper's entries. The one-off dispatch in `tests/unit/task-timeline-client.test.js` `runningTimeline` (records present, no `model`) needs the same treatment.

### Inside the area, larger
None.

### Outside the area
None.

## Close-out — LIN-4454

**Merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2425 (squash) as `c205190fdd0628e36f6fcfd26fb333f66a6a6e0b`, pinned with `--match-head-commit fcf75e915650a0758310de5936b91bbc922babc5`, the exact commit CI passed on. Deployed: the Harbour / production deployment of `c205190` reports success, and the page footer links `c205190`.

**How it meets what was asked:** review's account stands (Review comment ab3ea591). A dispatch's model is now the cost fold's answer, carried by `dispatchesOf` as `model: fold.last.model` (null with no records), and timeline rows read it. `dispatchModelOf` and its second ranking are retired, along with the Lessons clause that named it and the matching Waiting entry (found by its text).

### Changes I made after the approval
- `fcf75e915` — answers the blind read's one inside-area, fix-sized find. The `d()` helper in `tests/unit/task-timeline-page.test.js` and the records-present dispatch in `runningTimeline` in `tests/unit/task-timeline-client.test.js` now carry `model: 'claude-opus-5-5'` as the last key, matching the wire shape. They had been built with only `byModel`, a shape the read no longer produces. Test-only change, no assertion changed. The blind read's other sections were empty.

### Ledger (What CI Did Not Prove)
- **Inside — Lessons/Waiting edits surviving a LIN-4457 rebase:** conditional on LIN-4457 landing first. It did not: PR #2424 (`feat/lin-4457-cost-read-calls-file`) was still open and unmerged when this merged, so by review's own rule the item passes to LIN-4457's rebase. I have left a comment on LIN-4457 with the exact checks (no `dispatchModelOf` tail on the Lessons line, its own Lesson still present, no Waiting entry naming `dispatchModelOf`, Lessons under 6,144 bytes, CI green on the rebased head). Nothing on this ticket is left undone.
- **Outside:** none (review found none; the "should `byModel` carry `pricedUsd`" question already points at piece 7, LIN-4457). Gate tickets filed: none. Existing-ticket check: nothing to file, so nothing to link.

### Verification
- **Final CI on `fcf75e915`:** all 8 checks pass (`CI success`, Unit, Unit proxy/clock +400d, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan). Run https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/43453731195. Locally the 5 affected test files passed, 67 pass and 0 fail, before the push.
- **On what landed:** `GET /api/proxy/issues/LIN-4454/cost` on the deployed Harbour returns `dispatches[]` entries whose last keys are `lastRequestAt, model`. The single-dispatch lanes (blind-read, review, scoping, survey-place, survey-task) show the same model on the lane and the row. The deployed `/instructions` carries the new `(LIN-4454) model` wording.
- **Post-deploy steps not run:** none were named.

### Housekeeping
- Parent LIN-4447: no code-driven departure from the approved plan, so no comment there. The ticket's "Settles Waiting: 19" was stale (entry 20 after LIN-4453); the PR removed the right entry by its text, as the surveys said.
- The builder's `### Leftovers` / `Retires:` comment was not posted; review accepted the PR's "What this piece retires" section as equivalent, and nothing here needed it.
- Description archived and pruned (see below if the archive could not be confirmed).

## Autopilot run summary: LIN-4454 (stepper)

**Outcome:** merged, deployed, Done. PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2425, squash-merged as `c205190fdd0628e36f6fcfd26fb333f66a6a6e0b` (pinned to head `fcf75e915650a0758310de5936b91bbc922babc5`, all 8 CI checks green; I re-read the check runs on that commit myself).

**Step sequence (converging, no repeats):** survey-task → survey-place → scoping (just the task, no cuts, standing policy) → implementation (stepped, 4 beats, one warm session) → review (conditional Approve) → blind-read (better) → close-out.

**Implementation beats:**
1. Re-ground at cfd152fa4, branch, witness test written first and watched to fail 3/3 on unchanged code (commit `d04613850`).
2. `dispatchesOf` carries `fold.last.model` (last key; `null` with no records), timeline rows read it, `dispatchModelOf` deleted; witness passes 4/4; two mutation checks red; full unit suite 25,283/25,283 (`06d183ae1`). Case 4 added to rule out the `byModel[0]` shortcut.
3. Waiting entry (found by text; the ticket's "19" was stale, it was 20) and the Lesson clause removed; Lessons 4,269 → 4,182 bytes (cap 6,144); shape docs updated (`0b41e6d6d`).
4. PR #2425 opened, CI green, summary comment.

**Checks I made rather than took on report:** survey/scoping/review/blind-read comments exist on the ticket; PR state and CI rollup via `gh`; the close-out fixture commit `fcf75e915` is test-only, one added `model` key in each of two fixtures, no assertion changed.

**Retired:** `dispatchModelOf` and its ranking, the Lesson clause naming it, the Waiting entry about it.

**Left for others:** the review's one ledger item (docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md rebase check) applies only to whichever of this PR and LIN-4457 (#2424) lands second. LIN-4457 landed second, so close-out left that ticket a comment listing the checks. Not this ticket's to settle.

**Engine note:** after the review, the engine dispatched `blind-read` before `close-out`. I rode it out (read-only, no demonstrable miss) and did not override the verb.

description:
## As asked

**Parent:** LIN-4447 (Runs & dispatch, left simpler). The parent's scope is its `## As asked` block. Its approved design and plan are the `## Design` and `## Implementation Plan` sections of the parent description, and the Design comment (6efb91fa) holds the full analysis. **Start from the parent's approved plan and follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so in a comment on LIN-4447.**
**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer. **Grounding commit:** `origin/main` 4b5001ddf. On 2026-11-13 at 14:00Z it was still HEAD, with nothing landed since the ticket was filed.

## Piece 3 (small): one rule for a dispatch's model

**Cause:** `lib/task-timeline.js` `dispatchModelOf` (line 54) ranks models by its own rule. The cost figures use the fold's answer. `dispatchesOf` in `lib/cost-read.js` runs `foldRequestUsage(owned)` per dispatch but drops its `last`.

**Approach:** `dispatchesOf` carries `fold.last.model`, and timeline rows read that value.
**Retires:** `dispatchModelOf` and its ranking, plus the Lesson clause that names it ("a per-dispatch figure is the fold's answer" stays as the rule). **Settles Waiting:** 19.

**Testing / witness:** turn the Drift case (row 150) into a test. Model A has $5 priced plus one unpriced request, and model B has $1 priced: the lane and the timeline row must name the same model. With nothing priced, both must name the latest model.
Note: piece 7 also touches `lib/cost-read.js` (it moves `readCalls`/`callsSurfaceOf` out). Whichever piece lands second rebases. Pieces 3, 6 and 7 may share one session, but each gets its own PR.

Session fit: fits one session
Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4447's approving plan-review (comment 12619798-1986-467f-b67c-8bed766a7813, rev 2)

**Binding for every piece (from the parent's Constraints):** compute readiness from the trail on read and never store it. Add no GitHub or provider reads. In the same change, remove the Waiting entries this piece settles and any stale Lesson clause in `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`, and keep Lessons under 6,144 bytes. Say in the PR what this piece retires. Never recompute stored pre-cutover history, and never edit recorded prompt changelog text. The LLM & prompts side of the seam belongs to LIN-4448 (A14).

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** Each dispatch carries the cost fold's own model answer and the timeline's second ranking is retired, so one rule names a dispatch's model; nothing the surveys found binds beyond this, since no other copy of the rule exists.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Implemented

Merged as PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2425](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2425>) (`c205190fdd0628e36f6fcfd26fb333f66a6a6e0b`), deployed to production. The plan was implemented as approved, with no departure from LIN-4447's plan. A dispatch's model is the cost fold's answer (`fold.last.model`), carried on each dispatch and read by timeline rows. `dispatchModelOf`, its ranking, its Lessons clause and its Waiting entry are retired. The surveys' full analysis, the review, the blind read and the close-out summary are in the comment trail, and the earlier description is preserved in the task snapshots.
